target.title: fix(agents): tighten bash-tools schema fields from Type.Number to Type.Integer
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`bash-tools.schemas.ts` uses `Type.Number` for three fields that semantically require integer values — `yieldMs` (milliseconds), `offset` (log position), and `limit` (entry count). Fractional values like `offset=10.5` or `limit=5.3` silently pass schema validation and reach tool logic with nonsensical values.

## Root Cause

`Type.Number` in TypeBox accepts any JavaScript number including floats. For fields whose semantics are inherently integer-valued, this means invalid input survives the schema gate.

## Fix

Change three `Type.Number` to `Type.Integer` in `src/agents/bash-tools.schemas.ts`:

- `yieldMs`: milliseconds before backgrounding (default 10000) — sub-millisecond yields are not a practical use case
- `offset`: log position offset — fractional byte positions make no sense
- `limit`: log entry count — fractional counts make no sense

This mirrors the same pattern already applied to `lsSchema`, `grepSchema`, `toolSearch`, `readSchema`, and `processSchema` (lzyyzznl #105827, #105822, #105567, #105564, #105560).

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/agents/bash-tools.schemas.ts` | 3× `Type.Number` → `Type.Integer` |

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — Type.Integer rejects floats at the schema gate

TypeBox `Type.Integer` uses `Number.isInteger()` internally. Before the fix, `Check(schema, { offset: 10.5 })` returns `true` — the invalid value passes validation. After the fix, the same check returns `false` — the float is rejected before any tool logic runs.

### Vitest

Existing agent tool schema tests continue to pass. The change is a schema-level tightening that does not affect any runtime behavior for valid integer inputs.

```
✓ All existing bash-tools schema tests pass unchanged
```
